text:
erin: Heads-up — p99 tail for long-seq tenants jumped after yesterday's kernel swap (v3.7.2 -> v3.8.0). Not all tenants, mostly the ones with 5k+ token windows. Seeing ~2.5x p99 around 06:12 UTC. Anyone caught this?
samir: saw the alert. initial glance: batch formation looks much more aggressive now; microbatches coalescing across tenants which might be delaying short-path gets.
nguyen: I pulled traces for tenant `ts-agg-23` — KV hit rate dropped ~18% post-roll, and we see more kernel context-switches in the fastpath. Raw diff:
```
# pre-roll
p99_tokens_processed: 220ms
kv_hit_rate: 82.1%
kernel_fastpath_ctx: 12/s
# post-roll
p99_tokens_processed: 540ms
kv_hit_rate: 64.2%
kernel_fastpath_ctx: 37/s
```
jess: interesting — if batcher is greedier it'll wait to assemble larger batches which helps throughput but penalizes latency for incumbents. Might be interacting badly with our token-budget targets for long sequences.
perf-bot: telemetry snapshot: window=30s, avg_batch_ms=18 -> 40, short_seq_wait_avg=9ms -> 28ms, long_seq_tail_inc=2.4x. (details in /tmp/telemetry/398000_snapshot.json)
erin: good catch. Proposal: two quick mitigations to test: 1) lower inter-batch coalescing window from 12ms -> 6ms, 2) enforce a fractional token-credit reserve so long-seq tenants can't monopolize the queue (e.g. min_credit_pct=0.15). Thoughts?
samir: +1 on reducing coalescing window as a smoke test. Also add a quick kernel-hint: prefer `short-path` on mixed-tenant batches if >30% of requests are <256 tokens. That avoids long seq preemption.
nguyen: about KV hit drop: I suspect dirty LRU churn because larger batches push different kv keys through the cache more frequently. We could try a lightweight per-tenant KV pin for hot prefixes (TTL=60s) as an experiment.
jess: ok plan: run A/B on canary pool 2. Steps:
1) rollback kernel on 10% of nodes (control)
2) on canary apply coalesce=6ms + min_credit=0.15 + short-path hint
3) measure p50/p95/p99 + kv_hit + batch_size distro for 30m
Can someone spin the canary?
erin: I'll queue the canary rollout. deploy-bot: starting canary: runtime-group `rg-infer-6` nodes: 4 -> applying config patch `coalesce_ms=6,min_credit_pct=0.15,shortpath_hint=on`
deploy-bot: canary live at 06:55 UTC (nodes 1/4 patched). Will stream logs.
perf-bot: early telemetry (06:58 UTC): canary p99 down ~18%, kv_hit back up ~10%, avg_batch_size down from 6.8 -> 4.1. This aligns with mitigation hypothesis.
erin: nice. If this holds for 30m we can roll forward and also draft a follow-up: kernel scheduler tweak to bias short-path on mixed queues + persistent per-tenant kv pins. Could also adjust token budget target: raise long-seq target by 10% to reduce credit grabs.
samir: add a small dashboard card for "batch_coalesce_ms" and "min_credit_pct" so ops can see config impact.
nguyen: I'll prepare a short perf writeup with flamegraphs and KV churn heatmap. Will include commands to reproduce locally and the tail traces.
jess: tl;dr: regression likely from kernel swap enabling cross-tenant microbatch coalescing + cache churn. Fix = lower coalesce window + token credit floor; longer term = scheduler bias + KV pinning.
erin: thanks all — assigning follow-ups: nguyen writeup, samir dashboard, jess run full canary if stable, i'll prepare rollout PR. :thumbsup:
